extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and psychometricians developing or evaluating measurement instruments and inter-rater reliability studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical examples for measuring and interpreting inter-rater reliability and validity of clinical/behavioral assessment tools (use of kappa, ICC, percent agreement, tool development and validation steps). Applicable to clinicians and researchers designing, testing, or choosing assessment instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chamberlain's percent positive agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Chamberlain's percent positive agreement used to compare diagnoses and comorbidities between two data abstractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as percent positive agreement per diagnosis/comorbidity (examples: ICU primary and other admitting diagnoses ranged 0%–71%; comorbidities 40%–100%). Useful for measuring agreement on presence (positive classification) when prevalence and asymmetry affect kappa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's kappa statistic (unweighted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohen's kappa used to calculate interrater reliability for categorical/nominal variables (e.g., diagnosis present/absent, classification decisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (kappa values of 0.93, 0.73, 0.75, 0.80 for different case definitions). Use kappa to quantify agreement beyond chance; present kappa with interpretation and confidence intervals when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted Cohen's kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Weighted kappa (Kw) used for ordinal scales and to account for degrees of disagreement (e.g., RASS, NDE Scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: weighted kappa values roughly ≥0.90 between nurses and physicians for RASS; NDE Scale inter-rater Kw 0.77 and test–retest Kw 0.96. Use when categories are ordered and partial agreement should be weighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICC used to assess reliability for continuous or interval-level measures (e.g., acute physiology points, predicted probability of mortality, instrument scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ICC 0.88 for acute physiology points, ICC ranges 0.81–0.95 for pelvic inclinometer measures; interpret ICC magnitude (moderate, good, excellent) and specify model type (e.g., ICC(2,1)). Report CIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent (raw) agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw percentage agreement between raters (simple proportion of identical ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: overall inter-rater agreement 86.2% in periodontal scoring; intrarater reliability 91.5%. Useful as descriptive metric but should be used alongside chance-corrected measures (kappa) because it does not account for agreement expected by chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation thresholds for agreement statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Using qualitative descriptors (poor, moderate, substantial, strong, excellent) to interpret kappa/ICC values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page examples: race kappa 0.81 described as strong, age points 0.95 strong, chronic health points 0.50 moderate, Glasgow Coma Score 0.36 poor; weighted kappa ≥0.90 described as near-equal agreement. Report descriptors with numeric values and context-dependent caveats (clinical vs. aggregate use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Staged tool development and validation process
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-step approach to develop assessment instruments: item generation; mapping to theoretical constructs; expert review for content validity; inter-rater reliability testing; pilot testing; psychometric testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CACTiM (reflection) followed this staged model (15-item scale). Use expert mapping and pilot samples before large-scale psychometrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content validity index (CVI) / expert review
rubrics_metrics.description: Use expert review and CVI to assess content validity of instrument items and overall scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CACTiM expert review produced a high CVI (0.98). Report CVI and describe expert panel and procedures used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal reliability (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess internal consistency of scales using Cronbach's alpha to indicate homogeneity of items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CACTiM reported Cronbach's alpha = 0.93 (good internal reliability). Report alpha for total scale and subscales and consider dimensionality before interpreting alpha.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct validity via factor analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use exploratory (or confirmatory) factor analysis to test whether item structure maps to hypothesized constructs (subscales/factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CACTiM's exploratory factor analysis revealed three factors: analyses context, reasoned inquiry, and self-evaluation. Report factor loadings, explained variance, and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent and convergent validity (correlations with related measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate validity by correlating instrument scores with other measures that assess similar constructs (e.g., self-reported pain, pain severity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: pain behavior frequencies correlated 0.46–0.53 with self-reported pain and 0.58 with self-reported pain behaviors; correlation between total observed behaviors and naïve observer ratings = 0.87. Report correlation coefficients and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant validity and sensitivity to change; ROC/AUC and cutoff selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess instrument’s ability to distinguish groups (discriminant validity) and detect change over time; use ROC AUC and suggest cutoff values where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: PICS distinguished patients with/without ICBs with ROC AUCs 0.92–0.95; cutoff values suggested. Provide ROC analyses, AUC, sensitivity/specificity, and justify cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and cultural adaptation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow standard translation/adaptation guidelines—translate, review for comprehensibility, and assess face validity—before reliability testing in new language versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Italian NDE Scale underwent staged translation and face validity review by palliative care team, then inter-rater and test–retest reliability assessment. Document translation steps, reviewers, and any back-translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater and test–retest reliability reporting (including CIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report inter-rater (and test–retest) reliability estimates with appropriate statistics (kappa, ICC) and confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Italian NDE Scale inter-rater Kw 0.77 (95% CI 0.67–0.87), test–retest Kw 0.96 (95% CI 0.91–1.00). Include sample sizes, number of raters, and number of observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-rater (repeat) reliability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess consistency within the same rater over time (intrarater reliability), often reported as percent agreement or ICC/kappa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: turbinate grading intrarater reliability 91.5% (95% CI 88.7–94.3). Include retest interval and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-category / item-level reliability reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reliability estimates for each category/item (e.g., κ per grade, kappa per diagnosis) rather than only overall statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: turbinate classification reported categorical κ for each grade (grade1 κ=0.8541, grade2 κ=0.7310, etc.); this helps identify items/categories with lower agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of data objectivity to reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that reliability depends on the objectivity of source data; more objective chart data yield higher reliability of abstracted elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reliability for ICU diagnoses and APACHE II elements related to objectivity of primary data in charts. Consider auditing and improving source-data objectivity to increase reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats for implicit (structured) peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured implicit peer review may yield moderate reliability for overall quality and preventable death assessment (kappa ~0.5) but poor agreement for many focused measures (kappa ≤0.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: implicit review adequate for aggregate comparisons (e.g., comparing wards) but inadequate for reliable evaluation of single patients with one or two reviewers. Be aware of systematic reviewer bias (harsh/lenient) affecting some measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of duplicate reviews, multiple raters, and rater training
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement duplicate reviews (percentage of double-rated cases), multiple raters, and rater training to estimate and improve reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: studies used duplicate reviews (20% duplicates), two independent raters, and trained raters (12 internists trained). Report training procedures and percent duplicates when reporting reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding of raters and limitations when absent
rubrics_metrics.description: Blinding raters to prior ratings or to other information is important; lack of blinding can inflate reliability estimates or produce bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example caution: pelvic inclinometer raters were not blinded; authors warned about interpreting test–retest reliability within a single session. Report blinding status and discuss impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using interrater reliability to infer validity for bias correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods exist to translate interrater agreement (e.g., kappa) into estimates of sensitivity and specificity for exposure classification and to correct bias in effect estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a Bayesian method uses kappas to estimate sensitivity/specificity and correct odds ratios for exposure misclassification; such approaches increase insight into misclassification and adjust uncertainty accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual reporting: sample, setting, and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report study design details (sample size, population, settings, recruitment methods, number of raters) and limitations that affect generalizability of reliability estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples across abstracts: convenience samples, specialist-center recruitment affecting generalizability, healthy-only participant samples limiting applicability. Always state limitations and intended inference scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended psychometric evidence package for new clinical tools
rubrics_metrics.description: A defensible validation package includes evidence of content validity (expert/CVI), inter- and intra-rater reliability, internal consistency, construct and concurrent validity, discriminant validity/sensitivity to change, and appropriate translation/adaptation steps if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from multiple instruments (CACTiM, PICS, NDE Scale, turbinate scale) illustrate this combination. Present multiple lines of evidence rather than a single reliability statistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control in large-scale scoring (need for external controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale assessments often implement external quality controls (monitoring, training, item-level checks) to guarantee interrater reliability; omission may jeopardize score quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example research question: can teachers reliably score national tests without monitoring/training? Consider implementing external controls to assure scoring consistency in high-stakes or large-scale contexts.
